findings.text: Same-moment fetch at ~10:03 ET loses the input-window tail to paper-feed store lag (7 minutes missing at fetch; present at 14:14:52Z re-request). The amendment-34 window ends 10:05 ET, so fetching later inside the window cannot wait out an ~11-minute publication lag; if this lag recurs on subsequent sessions, every prospective row will be recorded COLLECTED then EXCLUDED (g3_open_window_incomplete) at scoring, and the campaign accumulates zero evaluable sessions. Owner decision required for any timing change (amendment; auditor changed nothing). Interim: rows are lawful and honestly flagged.

COLLECTOR_STATE.json still carries script_sha256 ca5d0b96... (Lane-H collector at b8d52076) while the executed collector is 3451d380... (Lane K at 325c4030 == HEAD), and ledger_rows: 0 while the ledger has 2 rows: update_state_next_fire refreshes only next_fire/updated_utc. Auth 36 itself pre-declares this exact staleness as bookkeeping; the ledger's own sha-chain is intact and independently verified. Refresh at next full state write.

write_raw manifest sha-chain is inert: it reads prev line key 'sha256_of_line', but persisted manifest lines only carry 'sha256' (the 'sha256_of_line' key is added to the in-memory record AFTER the line is written), so prev_sha256_of_line is null forever (both of today's entries null). Per-file sha256 are correct and the raw files are committed at HEAD (git blob tamper-evidence), so today's evidence is unaffected; the law-9 chain intent is not realized for future sessions.
